html: The heart module is about order. Mice were exposed to aircraft noise for four days and only then had a coronary artery tied off, and the hearts that followed were worse: more myeloid cells, more Ly6C-high monocytes, more interleukin-6, interleukin-1 beta, CCL-2 and NOX2 in the tissue, poorer function. Before the infarction the circulating leucocytes had already changed, carrying more oxidase and more phosphorylated NF-kB, which is what the paper calls conditioning: the damage is not done by the noise, it is prepared by it. People in the population cohort who had been exposed and were annoyed by it had a worse ejection fraction after their infarction, which is the same statement in a different population. The map draws that chain where it is molecular. The transcription factor drives CCL2 in cardiac tissue, the chemokine is secreted and binds CCR2 on the monocyte, and the arriving cell makes superoxide through the oxidase it brought; mice without that receptor recruit far fewer such cells. Caspase-1 cuts pro-interleukin-1 beta into the cytokine that is measured. In the muscle itself the switch is the one the vessel already showed: the synthase is S-glutathionylated at every day of exposure, cardiac oxidase activity rises with it, and the uncoupled enzyme makes superoxide, which meets NO as peroxynitrite and leaves nitrated protein behind. That last one is drawn here and not in the brain module for a plain reason: in the heart it was measured.
